title: Relative local finite presentation for morphisms of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Interpret locally of finite presentation and locally of finite type by etale scheme charts, with scheme meanings as in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $g\circ f:X\to Z$ is locally of finite presentation and $g$ is locally of finite type, then $f$ is locally of finite presentation. No separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a scheme atlas $w:W\to Z$. Form $Y_W=Y\times_ZW$, choose a scheme atlas $v:V\to Y_W$, form $X_V=X\times_YV$, and choose a scheme atlas $u:U\to X_V$. These fibre products are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], so the atlases exist by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The atlas maps and the projections $Y_W\to Y$ and $X_V\to X$ are representable surjective etale, and so are their composites $b:V\to Y$ and $a:U\to X$, by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Let $q:V\to W$ and $h:U\to V$ be the remaining projections. The fibre-product identities give $g b=w q$ and $f a=b h$, hence $(g\circ f)a=w(qh)$. Thus $(V,W,b,w,q)$ is a presentation diagram for $g$, $(U,W,a,w,qh)$ is one for $g\circ f$, and $(U,V,a,b,h)$ is one for $f$, each with surjective source chart.

By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], local finite type and local finite presentation are etale local on source-and-target. Apply condition (1) of [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] to the first two presentation diagrams of step 1: the hypothesis on $g$ gives local finite type of the scheme map $q:V\to W$, and the hypothesis on $g\circ f$ gives local finite presentation of $qh:U\to W$. Apply [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation] with its base scheme $S=W$, source $X=U$, target $Y=V$, structure maps $p=qh$, $q=q$, and $h=h$. The equality $q\circ h=p$ is the definition of $p$. All three objects are schemes, and the two finiteness hypotheses have just been verified. It follows that $h:U\to V$ is locally of finite presentation.

In the third presentation diagram of step 1 the vertical maps $a:U\to X$ and $b:V\to Y$ are representable etale, $a$ is surjective, and step 2 proves local finite presentation of $h$. Local finite presentation is etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Condition (2) of [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] therefore proves that $f$ is locally of finite presentation in precisely the chart sense stipulated in the statement. The construction used unrestricted scheme atlases and no quasi-compactness or separation assumption.
